Risk officer call: refuse any size.

The brief shows a coin up 3,592x in 30 minutes with a market cap of $178M, which is implausible for a fresh pump.fun launch and points to bad or manipulated data. Even taken at face value, the structure is disqualifying: the top 5 buyers hold 99.9% of early flow, bundle share is 100%, 5,007 SOL came from 19 buyers in the first two minutes, and sell-to-buy in that window is 0.0005. This is a textbook operator setup, and the curve shows essentially no real two-sided market.

Pool depth (about 5,100 SOL) is ample for a $20 ticket, so liquidity is not the issue. The 30-second execution lag also makes a 20-50% stop unreliable on a coin this concentrated.

If the desk insists on any exposure, the sanity bounds would be the minimum $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold, but I recommend skipping. Skipping costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The case for buying GOIF now is weak, and I don't think the brief supports a buy.

The strongest points are real: 150 buyers and 54.2 SOL bought in the last 15 minutes, net flow of +22.9 SOL, the coin is alive, and it is up about 3,592% over 30 minutes. Pool depth of roughly 5,100 SOL means a $20 ticket would face little price impact.

But the demand story is undercut by the data. The first two minutes after graduation show 5,007 SOL bought by 19 buyers, with the top five buyers taking 99.9% and a launch bot present. That is operator concentration, not organic interest. The curve shows bundle share at 1.0 and top-3 share at 1.0. Recent sells (31.3 SOL, 30 sellers) show distribution is already happening, and the 15-minute return is essentially flat at +0.9%. Holding the 30-minute high is also no evidence of durability, since the drawdown is zero only because the peak is recent.

Against base rates, operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even, and the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost pushes expected value negative. Nothing here shows demand that will persist for 30-60 minutes. I recommend skipping.
